explanation: Norse settlers reached Iceland around 874. Polynesian voyagers, ancestors of the Māori, arrived in New Zealand about 400 years later, making it one of the last big lands people settled.

claims.text: Lasting human settlement of Iceland began around 874, with Norse settlers.
Polynesian ancestors of the Māori first settled New Zealand around 1250 to 1300.
New Zealand was one of the last major land masses to be settled by humans.

writerNotes: Self-check (CONTENT_GUIDE 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed in prose because this tooling's schema has no selfCheck field. Subtopic: exploration and encounters (settling new lands). Lint: content:check reports no errors on this item and no warnings. Claims: every checkable statement in the labels, values and explanation is listed; risk sits at or above the C26 floor (digits, number words, quotation marks, superlatives, only, first, named after, comes from, means), and the key claim is high because the item is counterintuitive. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers these historical facts, so checker A needs web evidence for every high-risk claim. Rival test: Players tend to picture the Pacific as settled long ago and Iceland as Viking-age, so many pick b. Irish monks may have reached Iceland even earlier, which only widens the gap; older claims of settlement in New Zealand before 1200 have been rejected by radiocarbon dating, so the 400-year margin holds. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: the people and events are covered in world history teaching and international reference works, so a player in Lagos, Mumbai, Toronto or Sydney starts level with one in London or Chicago. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, plain hyphens only, explanation of 30 words. Myths: screened every claim against content/reference/myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. Mystery and encore codes: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: The value 1280 sits in the middle of the accepted 1250 to 1300 range; the display gives the range. WebSearch: none used by the writer.
